summary: The old harness cannot reach the changed CHARBOUND and STRIPCC behavior.
missing_information: The delegated build script is not supplied, so full target and build coverage cannot be certified.

claims.necessity_reason: The harness maps text and directly normalizes UTF-32. A finite input containing a stripped control and surviving text can produce boundary markers. The after source preserves markers for surviving text and removes the marker before the stripped control, but no old-harness call combines CHARBOUND with STRIPCC or feeds one mapping result into another.

before.requirement: Retain boundary markers for surviving text and remove the marker before a control stripped by STRIPCC.
before.reason: The before normalizer strips negative boundary markers whenever STRIPCC is active, so it does not support this tuple.

source_evidence.dependency_reason: Defines STRIPCC and CHARBOUND as distinct options.

after.requirement: With CHARBOUND and STRIPCC, retain boundary markers for surviving text and remove the marker before a stripped control.
after.reason: The changed normalizer supports both marker actions. Mapping forwards its options through decomposition and reencoding, but the fixed harness never supplies both flags to one operation. Its calls all consume the original input, so they cannot form the equivalent two-step route.

source_evidence.dependency_reason: CHARBOUND inserts the negative boundary sentinel before a grapheme.
The mapping path passes the caller's options through decomposition and reencoding.
The added test supplies a finite combined-flags witness and demonstrates the equivalent two-step mapping sequence.

claims.comparison_reason: The same marker-retention and control-marker-removal tuple is assessed against the same old harness. It was unsupported before and is supported but unreachable through that harness after the change.
